context.title: A foreign woman's position
context.text: Medea lacks secure kinship and civic protection in Corinth. Exile would threaten the practical basis of her children's lives as well as her own.

context.title: The earlier voyage
context.text: Medea helped Jason obtain the Golden Fleece and left her home with him. Their competing accounts of that help shape their present dispute.
context.takeaway: Listen for who claims to owe whom.

notice.text: Compare persuasive speech with private deliberation.
notice.why: Medea does not tell every listener the same intention.
A clear grievance does not justify every possible act.

opening: Jason is leaving Medea to marry a princess and explains that the arrangement will benefit everyone. Medea has abandoned her country, betrayed her family, and borne his children; he would like her to understand the advantages of his new position. Euripides lets her answer with a clarity that makes his self-justification collapse. Then the woman whose grievance is so easy to recognise begins considering what she can still do with it. Her intelligence remains formidable as her intentions become harder to bear.
